Title: Anthony Loke’s transport push: LRT3 opens, ridership surges past one million, but congestion fight unfinished
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Nearly four years into his second stint as transport minister, Anthony Loke can point to gains in public transport and rail use, but says Malaysia’s growing vehicle population, ageing infrastructure and gaps in connectivity continue to complicate efforts to overhaul the country’s transport system.
One of the areas where Loke has sought to make the biggest changes is Prasarana Malaysia Berhad, which operates the Klang Valley’s Light Rail Transit (LRT), Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) and monorail services.
Loke said Prasarana was in poor shape when he returned to the ministry in late 2022, with frequent disruptions and maintenance problems affecting public confidence.
“Prasarana at the end of 2022 was in a really bad shape. And in terms of maintenance, in terms of a lot of disruption. Public confidence towards Prasarana was extremely low,” he told
Malay Mail
in an interview.
“Even simple things are not running. Escalators in the station are not running, the light bulbs are out, toilets are not functioning, trains disrupted and so forth,” he said.
Loke said his first act as minister was to conduct a spot check at an MRT station to signal his focus on Prasarana.
“That is to send a message, to set the tone and send a message. And I wanted to focus on Prasarana,” he said.
He subsequently made Prasarana a permanent feature of post-Cabinet meetings and required the company to report on key performance indicators, particularly maintenance and service disruptions.
“I made it a point that they have to report everything on the key parameters and the dashboard, and drove them to focus on maintenance,” he said.
The number of disruptions fell in 2024 and 2025, although the situation deteriorated again in early 2026, particularly on the ageing Kelana Jaya Line, while additional trains planned for the line have yet to arrive.
“By and large, compared to 2022, our scenario is in a better shape today in terms of the overall operations, in terms of the overall planning and management,” he said.
Rail use grows as vehicle numbers climb
The LRT3 Shah Alam Line at Johan Setia Station, Klang, June 28, 2026. — Picture by Firdaus Latif
Loke said the recovery in urban rail use to pre-Covid levels showed that public transport demand remained strong, with certain lines including the Kelana Jaya Line now facing overcrowding and ridership continuing to rise following the opening of the LRT3 Shah Alam Line.
“We have consistently surpassed one million in daily ridership.
“But the growth in rail use is happening alongside a continuing increase in vehicles on Malaysian roads.
“But can you imagine without that the rail system, the traffic will be even worse off, right?” he said.
Malaysia recorded more than 700,000 vehicle sales last year, Loke said, reflecting a structural problem that has made it difficult to reduce congestion despite continued investment in public transport.
“This is a structural issue which not many people would understand, you know, people complain why traffic jam is still ongoing, without realising that the car population is increasing,” he said.
Loke said Malaysia’s automotive policy had encouraged vehicle ownership but lacked a corresponding policy to take older cars off the road.
“The car population will increase every day,” he said.
However, he said introducing an end-of-life vehicle policy would be difficult because many Malaysians still depend on older cars, particularly in semi-urban areas.
“And in our country, it’s not that practical yet, because not everyone can afford to get a newer car,” he said.
“And there is a real need for vehicles, especially in the semi-urban areas.
“Malaysia’s dispersed population also means public transport cannot reach every corner of the country.
“The fact is that, public transport cannot reach every corner of the country,” Loke said.
Bridging the first and last mile
The ministry has sought to address that gap through Demand Responsive Transit (DRT) services operated by Prasarana in the Klang Valley, alongside feeder buses linking residential areas with rail stations.
Loke said there were about 380 points for DRT services, but landed housing areas, particularly on the outskirts of the Klang Valley, remained difficult to serve.
“On the outskirts of Klang Valley, we have a lot of landed properties, and landed housing estates, which make it difficult for the last mile and first mile to reach every corner in every household,” he said.
“We know, for example, the buses, they will not be able to serve every single lane or every single house in the housing estates.”
The ministry has also sought to encourage carpooling and ride-sharing, but Loke said the varied needs of commuters meant there was no single solution.
“We try multiple approaches, but there will not be a one-size-fits-all kind of solution,” he said.
Loke said the ministry has also sought to encourage carpooling and ride-sharing, but the varied needs of commuters meant there was no single solution. — Picture by Yusof Isa
Moving more cargo onto rail
Beyond moving passengers, Loke wants to make greater use of Malaysia’s railway network to transport cargo, with the ministry acquiring more locomotives, refurbishing older ones and adding wagons to increase freight capacity.
The government is also pushing for a rolling stock leasing programme between Malaysia and China to secure more trains and enable additional passenger services.
Loke said the railway network was a strategic national asset that had not been fully utilised.
“Railway is actually a very strategic asset of the country, which in the past we have not really fully utilised,” he said.
With the double-track railway network, the upcoming East Coast Rail Link and other upgrading projects, the government wants to create a rail artery across the peninsula for both passengers and cargo.
“We want to have this artery of transport network throughout peninsula so that we can connect the entire peninsula by railway, not only just for passengers but also for cargo,” he said.
The network would also connect major ports including Port Klang, Penang Port and Port of Tanjung Pelepas.
One project the ministry is pushing for is the Southern Bypass Line, which would connect Seremban directly to Port Klang and allow cargo trains from the south to bypass Kuala Lumpur.
Loke said freight trains from the south currently had to pass through Kuala Lumpur before heading to Port Klang, creating a bottleneck as cargo services shared the network with passenger trains.
If approved by the Ministry of Economy and Ministry of Finance, he said, the bypass would allow cargo from the south to travel directly to Port Klang.
Road safety remains a priority
Road safety, particularly involving heavy vehicles, has also taken up a significant part of the ministry’s work, with two major tragedies last year intensifying scrutiny of public service and heavy vehicles.
“Two tragedies happened within a month, which, you know, caused a lot of public concern and debate,” he said.
The ministry subsequently rolled out measures including stricter enforcement and regulation, new safety technologies and wider use of telematics systems.
Loke acknowledged that the measures came at a cost to operators and faced industry pushback, but said safety could not be compromised.
“But, safety is something which we have to deal with seriously,” he said.
Airfares remain largely market-driven
On airfares, Loke said the government had limited room to intervene as ticket prices were largely determined by market forces. — Picture by Yusof Isa
On airfares, Loke said the government had limited room to intervene as ticket prices were largely determined by market forces.
Malaysia does not have a policy of capping airline ticket prices except during selected major festive periods for flights between Peninsular Malaysia and Sabah and Sarawak, with the fare cap applying for about 12 to 14 days a year during major festivals including Chinese New Year, Hari Raya, Gawai and Christmas.
“We can’t afford to cap the fares every day,” he said.
Loke attributed higher airfares partly to increased jet fuel prices, which he said had risen by 30 to 40 per cent, as well as airlines cutting capacity because of higher operating costs.
“To be fair to the airlines, most airlines are trying to keep flying, even though they have some reduction in capacity, but overall it’s not that many,” he said.
The ministry has been engaging airlines to maintain basic connectivity while encouraging them to restore capacity, with most airlines agreeing to review their normal flight schedules by September and October.
“We have tried to encourage the airlines to slowly bring back their capacity,” Loke said.
For Loke, however, the work across Malaysia’s transport sector has no clear endpoint.
“Public transport is a never-ending effort,” he said.
“It’s not that we have done this and it’s finished.”

Title: Uncharted territories: Anthony Loke on alliances, unity constraints and search for lasting model
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 14 — Malaysia is still searching for a permanent model of governance eight years after the collapse of the country’s decades-old political order, with parties continuing to adjust to shifting alliances and electoral calculations, Transport Minister Anthony Loke said.
Loke, who is also DAP secretary-general, said the political landscape had gone through multiple permutations and collaborations since 2018, with political actors continuing to work out arrangements they believe could strengthen their positions.
“As I say, we are into uncharted territories right now,” he told
Malay Mail
in an interview.
“After the collapse of the decades-old model in 2018, I think we are still trying to find a permanent model, a permanent model of governance in Malaysia,” he said.
Loke said political parties and politicians would continue making calculations based on their chances of winning elections and remaining in power.
“Political parties and politicians will continue to calculate their function. They want to maximise their political function,” he said.
“And I think from 2018 until now, we have experienced different permutations, different calibrations.
“But as far as I’m concerned, I think it’s not going to end soon. So this will keep evolving,” he said.
Balancing party and government
The shifting political landscape has also left Loke navigating the competing demands of his roles as DAP secretary-general and Cabinet minister in the Unity Government, where the party works alongside former political rivals including Barisan Nasional.
Asked whether DAP had changed after becoming part of the government, Loke said the party had not abandoned its positions, but had to operate within the constraints of a unity government.
“No (the party has not changed). Of course, we need to coordinate, we need to work within the constraint of a unity government,” he said.
Loke said DAP leaders would continue articulating the party’s positions, while ministers had to observe collective responsibility within the Cabinet.
“As a secretary-general, of course I have to carry the position of the party, but at the same time I’m leading the Cabinet, so I have to carry that expression in the government.
“So I have to play that role in a very challenging way,” he said.
He said this meant he could not publicly criticise Cabinet colleagues, coalition parties or government policy while serving as part of the administration.
The shifting political landscape has also left Loke navigating the competing demands of his roles as DAP secretary-general and Cabinet minister in the Unity Government, where the party works alongside former political rivals including Barisan Nasional.
Transport Minister. — Picture by Yusof Isa
“Being part of the government, say for example, I cannot criticise another Cabinet member or the parties that are within the coalition government, that will be out of line in terms of collective responsibility,” he said.
“Nor can I criticise the government’s policy, because I’m part of the government,” he said.
At the same time, Loke said DAP could still take positions critical of government policies or actions, creating a delicate balance for the party as it remains part of the ruling coalition.
“But at the same time, sometimes the party takes a different position, and takes a position which is critical to the government’s policy or government’s action.
“So this is a situation where we have to face,” Loke said.
Loke said major decisions would continue to be brought before DAP’s Central Executive Committee (CEC) so the party could reach a common position.
“As far as I know, I mean any major decision will be brought back to the Central Executive Committee (CEC) for a common opinion or common position and a common decision that will be made by the CEC,” he said.
Political alliances will keep changing
Loke acknowledged that some political developments could be disappointing, but said parties would continue making decisions based on their electoral interests as Malaysia adjusts to its post-2018 political reality.
The shifting relationship between PH and BN was evident in the state elections, with the two federal coalition partners contesting separately in Johor and Negeri Sembilan.
In Johor, BN contested all 56 seats on its own, with state leaders citing the state’s political circumstances and grassroots views. PH subsequently announced it would also contest all 56 seats.
In Negeri Sembilan, BN initially remained open to working with PH but later decided to contest independently after PH announced it would contest all 36 seats
“This is something which is disappointing, but it happens.
“We have to, we just have to soldier on. We have to keep the faith alive,” Loke said.
He said political actors would continue searching for a governing arrangement that would put them in control, but ultimately the direction of Malaysian politics would depend on voters.
“I think political parties, different political actors will continue to search for a model which everyone of course would hope that they are in charge, they want to be in control,” he said.
“I think the public has to realise what is at stake and we have to soldier on, but at the end of the day, it’s the choice of the voters.”

Title: No tyre marks, no crushed bones: Defence challenges eyewitness accounts in murder trial of senior cop accused of running down teen with Ativa
Article:
IPOH, Aug 13 — The High Court here today heard that 17-year-old Muhammad Zaharif Affendi Muhd Zamrie was not run over by the vehicle driven by senior police officer DSP Mohd Nazri Abdul Razak, as claimed by eyewitnesses.
In his submission at the close of the prosecution’s case before Judge Datuk Bhupindar Singh Gucharan Singh Preet, lead defence counsel M. Athimulan argued that the “run over” theory was inconsistent with objective forensic and medical evidence.
He pointed out that the forensic pathologist had confirmed that the victim’s injuries were not consistent with being run over, as there were no crushed bones, destroyed organs, or tyre marks on the deceased’s body or clothing.
“My Lord, we respectfully submit that this medical evidence is a scientific and objective truth; it is not prone to the fallibility of human perception. It directly refutes the eyewitnesses’ core claim,” he submitted.
He contended that the eyewitness accounts were inherently unreliable because they were contradicted by expert medical evidence.
Athimulan said the absence of tyre marks on the deceased’s body and shirt supported the defence’s submission that the incident was a tragedy in which the teenager was “thrown” from the motorcycle upon contact, rather than intentionally “run over”, with the injuries suffered being consistent with a fall on the road.
He said the medical evidence completely ruled out all probabilities of the ocular evidence (direct oral testimony of an eyewitness) being true and, therefore, the defence counsel team respectfully submitted that the ocular evidence should be rejected.
“The eyewitness’s testimonies were flawed with perception of a traumatic event and influenced by social media impact,” he said.
Furthermore, Athimulan addressed the critical implications from the failure to tender “black box” (Event Data Records – EDR) data from the Perodua Ativa, particularly as the data was central to reconstructing the incident and determining mens rea (intent) under Section 300 of the Penal Code.
“It is respectfully submitted that, without black box data, the prosecution cannot prove whether the accused attempted to brake, or the accused swerved, or tried to avoid the collision, and whether the speed was consistent with loss of control rather than deliberate aim.
“My Lord, we are submitting that these are not minor gaps, but they are central to the prosecution’s theory of malicious intent. The charge against the accused is a most serious crime under the Penal Code, alleging murder by means of intentional vehicular conduct,” Athimulan said.
Deputy public prosecutors Afzainizam Abdul Aziz, Nasrul Hadi Abdul Ghani and Monisha Pandey appeared for the prosecution.
The accused was represented by a legal team comprising Athimulan, Datuk Mior Faridalathrash Wahid and Aiman Hakim Kamaruzzaman.
The trial will resume at 10 am tomorrow.
Mohd Nazri was charged under Section 302 of the Penal Code with causing the death of Muhammad Zaharif Affendi near Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan Jati on Dec 15, 2023, between 11.55 am and 12.32 pm.
The offence is punishable with either a death penalty or imprisonment of between 30 and 40 years, plus a minimum of 12 strokes of the cane if the death penalty is not imposed, upon conviction. — Bernama

Title: ‘I’m still in the Unity Govt’: Lahad Datu MP Yusof Apdal says viral resignation claim ‘untrue and malicious’
Article:
LAHAD DATU, Aug 13 — Deputy Science, Technology and Innovation Minister Datuk Dr Mohammad Yusof Apdal today denied claims that he had resigned and withdrawn from the federal government.
In a statement to Bernama today, he said the claim circulating on social media was untrue and malicious.
“I remain a member of the Unity Government administration and continue to carry out the trust and responsibilities entrusted to me,” he said.
He said the dissemination of such false information not only misled the public, but was also intended to tarnish his reputation.
Mohammad Yusof, who is also the Lahad Datu Member of Parliament from Parti Warisan, urged the public not to spread unverified news and to always refer to official sources for accurate and authentic information.
Today, a social media post circulated claiming that Mohammad Yusof had decided to resign as Deputy Minister, effective today. — Bernama

Title: If it feels like this haze has been here forever, you’re right — and 10 areas in Klang Valley and Sarawak are still recording unhealthy air pollution levels
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — A total of 10 areas nationwide recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4pm today, according to the Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS).
In Sarawak, seven areas recorded unhealthy readings, namely Serian with an API reading of 178, Samarahan (177), Kuching (174), Sri Aman (162), Sarikei (157), Mukah (152) and Sibu (151).
In the Peninsula, three areas also recorded unhealthy readings, namely Johan Setia (154) and Shah Alam (108) in Selangor, as well as Cheras (127) in Kuala Lumpur.
Meanwhile, 56 areas recorded API readings at the moderate level, while two areas recorded good readings.
API readings of between zero and 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are categorised as hazardous.
API data is released hourly based on readings from 68 air quality monitoring stations nationwide. — Bernama

Title: RM19,000 in alleged bribes lands Pahang agency official in MACC custody
Article:
KUANTAN, Aug 13 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has detained a female official from a government agency in Pahang over allegations of soliciting and receiving around RM19,000 in bribes to help secure tenders and contracts at another agency in the state.
Sources said the woman, in her 30s, was detained at about 6.45pm yesterday while giving a statement at the Temerloh MACC office.
“Preliminary findings suggest the suspect carried out the acts between 2016 and 2021, receiving bribes from various companies and individuals directly into her personal bank account,” the source disclosed.
The woman has been remanded for five days until Aug 19 after Magistrate Anis Adlina Abu Johan granted an application by the MACC at the Kuantan Magistrate’s Court today.
Meanwhile, Pahang MACC director Mohamad Shukor Mahmud, when contacted, confirmed the arrest and said the case is being investigated under Section 16(a)(B) of the MACC Act 2009. — Bernama

Title: 1MDB strikes a deal to drop its civil suit against former CFO, trial continues for Najib and five others
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) and its former chief financial officer (CFO) Radhi Mohamad have struck a deal today to withdraw the US$5.64 billion civil suit against him, with both parties agreeing to record a consent order in court.
1MDB counsel Lee Shih confirmed that Radhi, 55, and the plaintiffs, 1MDB and its four subsidiaries, had reached an agreement on the terms of the consent order and would file it in court today.
“My Lord, I can confirm that the plaintiffs and the sixth defendant would like to record a consent judgment or consent order today.
“Under the consent order, the suit against Radhi would be discontinued, with no liberty to file afresh,” he submitted.
The matter was subsequently confirmed by Radhi’s lawyer Datuk M. Reza Hassan.
After hearing submissions, High Court Judicial Commissioner Mohamad Redzuan Idrus ruled that the sixth defendant should be struck out as a co-defendant in the proceedings.
“Much obliged to all the parties for taking the time to settle this matter,” he said.
The trial for the US$5.64 billion suit entered its eighth day today, with three witnesses for the plaintiffs having taken the stand so far.
The afternoon session of the proceedings was resumed with former 1MDB chief executive officer Datuk Shahrol Azral Ibrahim Halmi reading his witness statement.
1MDB and its subsidiaries – 1MDB Energy Holdings Limited, 1MDB Energy Limited, 1MDB Energy (Langat) Limited and Global Diversified Investment Company Limited, formerly known as 1MDB Global Investments Limited – filed the civil suit on May 7, 2021.
They named former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Tun Razak, 1MDB’s former finance director Terrence Geh Choh Heng, former executive director Casey Tang Keng Chee, former chief investment officer Vincent Beng Huat Koh, Radhi, former investment director Kelvin Tan Kay Jim, and former chief investment officer Nik Faisal Ariff Kamil, as defendants.
The writ of summons stated that the plaintiffs, among other things, accused the defendants of breach of trust, breach of statutory duty, abuse of power and conspiracy to misappropriate 1MDB funds.
The trial resumes on Monday. — Bernama

Title: Space, gas and more: Russia and Malaysia eye new areas to work together
Article:
VLADIVOSTOK, Aug 13 — Russia sees prospects for a partnership with Malaysia in the space industry, Russian Minister of Science and Higher Education Valery Falkov said on Thursday, reported Sputnik/RIA Novosti.
The fifth meeting of the Joint Russian-Malaysian Commission on Economic, Scientific, Technical and Cultural Cooperation opened in Vladivostok on Thursday.
“There are prospects for Russia-Malaysia partnership in the space sector. A Russian company has already built and launched a satellite for Malaysia into orbit,” Falkov, the commission’s co-chairman, told reporters.
Meanwhile, Malaysian Higher Education Minister Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abdul Kadir said that Russia and Malaysia also have significant opportunities for cooperation in the energy sector, including liquefied natural gas and liquefied petroleum gas. — Bernama-Sputnik/Ria Novosti

Title: K9 sniffer dog joins third-day search for missing 14-year-old in Kelantan river
Article:
KUALA KRAI, Aug 13 — K9 sniffer dog Frankie from the Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) headquarters has been deployed to assist the search and rescue (SAR) operation for 14-year-old student Mohd Rayyan Hakimi Mohd Yusmiza, who has been missing since Tuesday.
Kelantan JBPM Operations Division assistant director Mohd Fadhlizil Ikram Ahmad Pauzi said Frankie was deployed to search along the riverbank as the SAR operation entered its third day today for the teenager, who is feared drowned in Sungai Kelantan near Kampung Aur Duri here.
“The operation is focusing on searching along the river, in addition to diving at several locations identified as areas of interest.
“The Water Rescue Team (PPDA) has also been deployed to conduct diving operations,” he told Bernama at the scene here today.
He said today’s SAR operation had been expanded to a four-kilometre radius, involving 63 personnel and volunteers from JBPM, the Royal Malaysia Police, Malaysian Civil Defence Force, Malaysia Volunteer Corps Department and villagers.
Mohd Fadhlizil Ikram said 12 boats had also been deployed, while the PPDA operation involved six personnel from the Machang, Pengkalan Kubor and Pengkalan Chepa Fire and Rescue Stations.
“The SAR operation is facing several challenges, particularly strong river currents and rising water levels, which are hampering the movement of personnel and the search for the victim, especially along the riverbed,” he said.
Bomba k9 Frankie joins the search for missing 14-year-old student Mohd Rayyan Hakimi Mohd Yusmiza on Day Three in the vicinity of Sungai Kelantan near Kampung Aur Duri, Kuala Krai. — Facebook screengrab from Bernama Radio
A Bernama check at the scene today found rescue personnel and villagers continuing to search along the river by boat, while PPDA personnel conducted diving operations at several identified locations.
Family members and villagers were also at the scene, closely following the search for Mohd Rayyan, who remained missing after bathing in the river with his friend, Luth Naiman Mohd Noraziron, 14.
Luth Naiman’s body was found by PPDA personnel at 9.10am yesterday, about 100 metres from the location where the two were last seen. — Bernama

Title: Two airlines, one passport problem: Immigration explains the 10-year validity issue
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 13 — Only two airlines have so far been reported to be experiencing system issues when processing Malaysian passports with a validity period exceeding 10 years, Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said.
He said the issue was not related to foreign countries refusing to accept Malaysian passports, but stemmed from systems used by certain airlines.
“So far, the feedback we have received is that only two airlines are experiencing problems. But I am not sure if there are others that we have yet to receive information about,” he told a press conference here today.
He stressed that the department was not blaming the airlines as the systems were used globally, while other airlines had no problems processing Malaysian passports with validity periods exceeding 10 years.
Zakaria said the 10-year validity period for Malaysian International Passports would continue as usual and had never been discontinued.
Only the additional validity period exceeding 10 years had been temporarily suspended due to problems with the airlines’ systems.
He said an additional validity period of up to six months had previously been given to applicants who still had more than six months remaining on their old passports when applying for renewal.
“What we have suspended is the additional validity period exceeding 10 years.
“(Before this,) we took into account the remaining validity on their old passports before they were replaced. So, to avoid disadvantaging Malaysians who still had a substantial period remaining, we gave them an extra six months,” he said.
Zakaria said the Immigration Department was also offering free replacement of passports already issued with a validity period of 10 years and six months.
The department said yesterday that, with immediate effect, it had suspended the validity period of Malaysian International Passports exceeding 10 years until the issue was resolved with the airlines and the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO). — Bernama

Title: ‘You are lucky you didn’t end up as corpses’: Judge’s grim warning to couple who used a Melaka mosque mortuary for their affair
Article:
MELAKA, Aug 13 — When a former mosque caretaker and a cleaner turned a mortuary room into the setting for their secret affair, they never imagined a judge would remind them just how close they had come to sharing the fate of the dead they were meant to prepare.
The Melaka Syariah High Court today fined the pair RM5,000 each, in default 18 months’ jail, after they pleaded guilty to committing illicit sex inside the mortuary room of Masjid Al-Ibadah in Kampung Bukit Piatu,
The Star
reported.
“You are lucky you did not end up as corpses while committing the act. Otherwise, you could have been washed there straight away,” Judge Mawardi Che Man was quoted as saying before passing sentence.
The accused, former mosque caretaker Mohd Rafi Abu Samah, 48, a widower with four children, and cleaner Norhaslinda Hashim, 51, a married mother of eight, admitted to their respective charges.
The court heard that the pair had engaged in illicit sexual acts on multiple occasions in the mortuary room between January and April, though the prosecution brought only a single charge against each based on available evidence.
The offence took place between 8am and noon on an unspecified date in April, in a room set aside for the final cleansing of the deceased before burial.
Mawardi stressed that although the mortuary room stood apart from the main prayer hall, it remained within sacred mosque grounds.
“This is where the deceased undergo their final cleansing before burial. Instead, a grave sin was committed there,” he was quoted as saying.
The two accused were charged under Section 52 of the Syariah Offences Enactment (State of Melaka) 1991, which carries a maximum fine of RM5,000, imprisonment of up to 36 months, or both, upon conviction.
The case first came to light through an unexpected route, with police handing the pair over to the Melaka Islamic Religious Department’s enforcement division on June 4 following an initial report alleging rape.
Subsequent police investigations found that the sexual acts had been consensual and repeated.
Melaka Chief Syarie Prosecutor Wan Mahyuddin Wan Muhammad, assisted by Syarie prosecutor Radzwan Abdullah, urged the court to impose a deterrent sentence, citing the sanctity of the location and the duo’s positions as mosque personnel.
The pair were represented by Syarie lawyer Muhammad Ammar Yaser Ahmad Nazri from the National Legal Aid Foundation.

Title: Cough and flu remedies flying off the shelves as Sibu’s haze refuses to clear
Article:
SIBU, Aug 13 — The haze situation in Sibu remained at an unhealthy level today, with the Air Pollutant Index (API) recorded at 152 as of 4pm, unchanged from Wednesday.
Local pharmacist Juliana Ting said demand for cough and flu medication had surged amid the hazy conditions, although there had been no significant increase in demand for eye medication or inhalers.
“Cough, sore throat, flu, headache and fever are among the common health problems experienced by people during unhealthy haze conditions,” she said when met.
Ting said children, the elderly and people with respiratory illnesses were among those most vulnerable to the effects of haze.
She advised asthma and other respiratory disease patients to continue taking their medication as prescribed, monitor their symptoms closely and seek immediate medical attention if their condition worsened.
“Always bring your inhaler if you are asthmatic, especially when going outside,” she advised.
Ting said symptoms such as shortness of breath, chest pain, coughing up blood and wheezing should not be taken lightly and required immediate medical attention.
For those experiencing cough, sore throat or eye irritation, she advised the public to wear masks, reduce outdoor activities and drink sufficient water to stay hydrated.
She said N95 masks were more suitable for filtering fine particles from haze and offered better protection than ordinary masks.
“However, the mask is not 100 per cent protection against haze. It is important to wear it properly, covering both the nose and mouth,” she said.
Ting also cautioned the public against taking medication without proper advice and stressed the importance of checking for any allergies to the medication.
She advised asthma and lung disease patients to keep a sufficient supply of prescribed medication at home, but warned against purchasing cough medication, antibiotics, steroids or inhalers solely as a preventive measure without assessment by a doctor or pharmacist.
Her advice comes as Sibu continues to experience unhealthy air quality, with the API recorded at 152 at 4pm, underscoring the need for residents to minimise exposure to the haze. — The Borneo Post

Title: Fake names, dead phone numbers: How Customs unravelled a RM1m cannabis export plot at KLIA
Article:
SEPANG, Aug 13 — The use of fake sender and recipient addresses, as well as unreachable telephone numbers, was uncovered in an attempt to export 12.675 kilogrammes (kg) of cannabis buds worth RM1.014 million via courier service to a European country last July.
Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) Customs director Aspalila Ag Tuah said the addresses stated on the four packages containing the drugs were identified as being in the Klang Valley, but investigations found that the information was false.
“They used fake addresses and the telephone numbers could not be reached either,” she said at a press conference here today.
However, she said authorities were still investigating the country of origin of the cannabis buds, as Malaysia was not a producer of the drug.
On July 13, the Enforcement Division operations team seized four packages suspected of containing cannabis buds at a mail and courier centre branch.
She said an inspection found that the drugs were concealed in airtight transparent plastic bags placed inside children’s toy boxes and were believed to have been intended for export to a European country.
In a related development, she said the Customs Department was informed that two pieces of luggage containing 47.8 kg of cannabis buds worth RM3.824 million, seized on July 14, had been kept at the Lost and Found section of KLIA Terminal 1 for about a month before being inspected.
Aspalila said the luggage was supposed to have been carried on a flight from Kuala Lumpur to Langkawi but was left unclaimed for 30 days.
Asked whether closed-circuit television (CCTV) footage was being reviewed to identify the individual who left the luggage, Aspalila said all angles would be taken into consideration as investigations were still ongoing, including into the identity and nationality of the individual believed to be linked to the luggage. — Bernama

Title: As air quality turns unhealthy at Minden, Penang exco urges public to limit outdoor activities
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Aug 13 — Air quality in parts of Penang reached unhealthy levels today, with the Minden monitoring station recording an Air Pollutant Index (API) reading of 107 at noon before improving later in the afternoon.
Penang housing and environment committee chairman Datuk Seri S. Sundarajoo said the Minden station recorded an API reading of 107 at noon, followed by 103 at 1pm, both within the unhealthy category.
He said the reading subsequently dropped to 97 at 3pm, returning to the moderate category.
“From August 10 to 13, up to 3pm, air quality in Penang was generally in the moderate to unhealthy categories, with API readings ranging from 60 to 107,” he said in a statement today.
Sundarajoo said Penang had four automated air quality monitoring stations operated by the Department of Environment (DoE), located in Seberang Jaya, Seberang Perai, Minden and Balik Pulau.
He said monitoring trends showed that the Minden and Balik Pulau stations recorded readings ranging from 57 to 107, while Seberang Perai and Seberang Jaya registered readings of between 66 and 96.
Three of the four stations remained in the moderate category, while one recorded an unhealthy reading.
Sundarajoo said preliminary information from the Asean Specialised Meteorological Centre (ASMC) showed that 213 hotspots were recorded in Sumatra and another 835 in Kalimantan between August 9 and 11.
Hotspots were also detected in several Malaysian states.
He said the increase in hotspots in Sumatra and Kalimantan indicated more significant fire activity in the region.
“The number of hotspots cannot be used as the sole indicator to determine the level of air quality in Penang,” he said.
He said the impact on Penang depended on meteorological conditions, particularly wind direction and speed, atmospheric conditions and rainfall distribution.
“Based on the DoE’s current monitoring, weather conditions influenced by intermittent rainfall have also helped to maintain Penang’s air quality at good to moderate levels,” he said.
Sundarajoo said PM₁₀ was identified as the dominant pollutant during the monitoring period, although its concentration remained at moderate levels.
He advised the public to monitor official API readings through the DoE’s Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) rather than relying on unverified information circulating on social media.
He also urged the public to refrain from open burning, including burning rubbish, dry leaves and agricultural waste, and to immediately report such activities to the authorities.
“Reduce strenuous outdoor physical activities if API readings increase, particularly for sensitive groups such as children, senior citizens and individuals with respiratory health problems,” he said.
He advised the public to reduce the amount of time spent outdoors, keep windows and doors closed, and use appropriate face masks if air quality deteriorated or hazy conditions worsened.
Sundarajoo said the DoE and other relevant agencies would continue monitoring air quality and hotspot activity.

Title: Two directors in Perak plead not guilty to faking Socso job incentive claims
Article:
IPOH, Aug 13 — Two company directors pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court today to charges of submitting false documents under the Social Security Organisation’s (Perkeso) Daya Kerjaya 2.0 incentive claims two years ago.
Leong Chooi Ying, 47, and Phun Wing Kei, 31, entered their pleas after the charges were read separately before Judge Meor Sulaiman Ahmad Tarmizi.
Leong, a director of MS Solution Management Services and MN Tree Resources, is accused of submitting a false Employee Confirmation Form to a Perkeso officer with intent to deceive.
She allegedly committed the offences on March 14, 2024, and May 5, 2024, at Taman Sri Pengkalan.
Phun, a director of CKIN Management Services and Diligent Cleaning Solution, faces similar charges for submitting false forms to two Perkeso officers with the same intent.
He is accused of committing the offence at No. 30, Persiaran Rishah 25, Taman Silibin Ria, on April 15, 2024, and May 29, 2024.
Their charges were filed under Section 18 of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC), which carries a maximum 20-year prison term and a fine of not less than five times the false claim, or RM10,000, whichever is higher.
MACC prosecuting officer P. Rubina appeared for the prosecution. Lawyers Damian Yeo Shen Li and Lim Kwang Ching represented Leong and Phun, respectively.
Bail was set at RM7,000 for Leong and RM8,000 for Phun, with one surety each. They were also ordered to report to the MACC monthly, surrender their passports, and avoid contacting witnesses.
Both case mentions were set for Sept 17. — Bernama

Title: Govt to reassess Sosma, refugee policies against current needs, says home minister
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — The direction of the Security Offences (Special Measures) Act 2012 (Sosma) and the issue of refugees require in-depth scrutiny to ensure that policies and measures remain relevant to current developments and national needs, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail.
Saifuddin Nasution, who chaired a discussion on the two issues this morning, said neither should be viewed from a single perspective, but instead assessed by taking into account recent developments, challenges on the ground and possible approaches for the future.
“That is why discussion platforms like this are important. We want every measure taken not merely to address immediate needs, but to be practical, well-founded and suited to current circumstances,” he said in a Facebook post today.
Sosma, which was introduced in 2012, provides authorities with special measures to address security offences and replaced the Internal Security Act 1960 (ISA), which was subsequently repealed.
The legislation has previously come under scrutiny, with various parties calling for its repeal or review, particularly concerning its provisions and implementation.
Meanwhile, the issue of refugees, particularly those from Myanmar, has also attracted significant public attention in recent months, amid concerns over national security, humanitarian considerations and the management of refugee communities. — Bernama

Title: MACC’s KWAP eFishery probe is almost done at home — now it’s waiting on overseas banks
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 13 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) has so far found no evidence of criminal wrongdoing involving corruption or misappropriation in the Retirement Fund Incorporated’s (KWAP) RM163.4 million investment in Indonesian aquaculture firm eFishery.
MACC chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said, however, that the full findings would only be available after investigators obtained financial information and documents from overseas banks, including those in Singapore and Indonesia.
“To date, 19 individuals have been called to assist in the investigation and have had their statements recorded. They include officers from KWAP, the Finance Ministry and Khazanah.
“No arrests have been made as we have not found it necessary to do so at this stage. However, the investigation is still ongoing,” he told a press conference today.
Abd Halim said investigators were also working to obtain statements from identified witnesses who were currently overseas.
“It can be reported that the domestic investigation is almost complete. We are now awaiting procedures to obtain Mutual Legal Assistance from several countries.
“There should be no issue about the process, but it may take some time as certain legal procedures must be followed,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Malaysian police granted access to question pilot detained in Jakarta over drug case, says home minister
Article:
SUBANG, Aug 13 — Indonesian authorities have reportedly allowed Malaysian police investigators to question a Malaysian pilot detained on suspicion of drug trafficking after he allegedly flew from Kuala Lumpur International Airport (KLIA) to Jakarta with drugs in his luggage.
According to the
New Straits Times,
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said a Narcotics Crime Investigation Department team sent to Jakarta had been granted access to interview the suspect.
“From the beginning, our investigators were given access by the Indonesian authorities to interview the subject,” he was quoted as saying.
Saifuddin said the investigation was continuing and urged that the team be given time to complete its work.
He added that proposals to strengthen airport security, being studied by a multi-agency team, could be jointly presented with the transport minister at next week’s Cabinet meeting.
The 39-year-old pilot was detained at Soekarno-Hatta International Airport on July 28 after Indonesian authorities allegedly found 70,114 ecstasy pills and four grammes of methamphetamine in his luggage.

Title: Fresh fruit, veg and protein could soon be added to SARA aid, says Zahid
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 13 — Today’s 18th Executive Committee meeting of the National Cost of Living Action Council (NACCOL) conducted an in-depth review of the local white rice roadmap, which includes a transitional framework to cushion the impact on vulnerable groups.
Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi, who chaired the meeting, said tackling the cost of living must go beyond supermarket shelf prices to address production costs, supply chains, access to nutritious food, healthcare and education costs, and support for vulnerable groups.
“To address this, the meeting closely reviewed the path forward for local white rice, focusing on balancing the needs of consumers with the survival of local farmers and producers.
“Among the key proposals is a soft-landing transition via subsidised rice, aimed at safeguarding vulnerable households before broader policy changes take effect,” he said in a statement.
Ahmad Zahid said the meeting also agreed to propose expanding the scope of the Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) aid to include fresh produce, such as fruits, vegetables, and fresh protein, for consideration at the main NACCOL meeting chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
“This is an important step to ensure government support goes beyond helping people’s spending power to actively improving access to healthier diets,” he added.
The government is taking cost pressures on business, logistics, and agriculture seriously, he said, including the impact of geopolitical developments, uncertainty in West Asia, import compliance costs, and subsidy rationalisation on food production expenses.
“Continuous monitoring of global geopolitical risks, volatility in West Asia, regulatory compliance expenses for imports, and the effects of targeted subsidies on agricultural production costs is essential to prevent these factors from leading to inflationary pressures on consumers,” he stated.
He said relevant agencies had also been asked to refine existing mechanisms, including targeted assistance for farmers, fishermen, and affected groups.
On healthcare, Ahmad Zahid said the meeting reviewed the rollout of 11 Reset strategy initiatives designed to keep private healthcare costs in check while improving access and expanding treatment options for the public.
He noted that this measure aligns with the government’s integrated framework under the Cost of Living Action Plan 2030, which aims to address living expenses across multiple sectors in a coordinated manner rather than through piecemeal actions.
Meanwhile, the government remains committed to keeping education affordable so that cost never stands in the way of developing talent, he said.
“Based on a mapping of 13 tertiary education aid schemes, 62,937 Form Six and university students received assistance last year, amounting to RM589.6 million.
“Such support needs to be reinforced to ensure every child, regardless of background, gets a fair chance at higher education,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Bandar Utama murder trial: Teen in dock says sorry in court over schoolmate’s death
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 13 — A 15-year-old boy, on trial for the murder of a female student at a secondary school in Bandar Utama, Petaling Jaya, last year, expressed remorse over the incident while testifying in the High Court here today.
The teenager, who was ordered to enter his defence after the prosecution established a prima facie case, chose to give an unsworn statement from the dock.
“He said he was sorry for what happened that caused the death and so on,” defence lawyer Kitson Foong told reporters after the hearing before Judge Adlin Abdul Majid.
Earlier, Foong informed the court that the defence would rely on the expert testimony of a psychiatrist to support a claim of unsoundness of mind under Section 84 of the Penal Code.
Dr Ian Lloyd Anthony, from Hospital Bahagia Ulu Kinta, was called as an expert witness under Section 45 of the Evidence Act 1950, to testify on the teenager’s mental state, including the referral process, treatment and clinical findings.
Foong said the defence had questioned the expert on psychiatric terms, such as psychosis and schizophrenia, in addition to the written report already filed.
The final witness for today, the doctor, testified that the teenager had suffered from delusions and mental illness for about five years.
Foong added that the expert believed a long treatment gap could worsen mental illness, especially when it begins in childhood.
His testimony resumes this afternoon, including possible cross-examination, before the defence closes its case and presents submissions.
The teenager is charged with murdering a 16-year-old girl in a school toilet in Bandar Utama between 9.20am and 9.35am on Oct 14, 2025.
The charge under Section 302 of the Penal Code carries the death penalty. However, under Section 97(1) of the Child Act 2001, the death penalty cannot be imposed on offenders under 18 if convicted.
Instead, under Section 97(2) of the same Act, the court may order the offender to be detained for a period determined by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, the Sultan, or the Yang di-Pertua Negeri.
After the afternoon proceedings, Foong told reporters the court had heard that the teenager’s schoolmates knew him as “the boy who always wears the mask”, a post-Covid habit and a key point in the defence’s mental health argument.
Dr Ian testified that the boy was normal before the pandemic but showed drastic behavioural changes afterwards, Foong said.
He said some classmates had never seen his face until the day of the incident, and at home, he reportedly covered his face with his shirt when speaking to family.
Dr Ian’s interviews with teachers and classmates confirmed the boy was normal pre-pandemic, with changes emerging only after that period, Foong added.
“The psychiatrist said the symptoms appeared post-Covid. Mask-wearing was necessary during Covid, but he kept it on even after, right up until the incident,” Foong said.
He added that the defence views the teenager’s actions and reactions before, during and after the incident, including his arrest and the course of the investigation, as strong supporting evidence of mental disturbance.
However, he said, the specific type of mental illness afflicting the teenager cannot yet be disclosed, as the court has yet to rule on the admissibility of the expert’s testimony.
Foong said his client is still receiving treatment and taking medication to control his emotions and delusions, and has been told he will need to continue the medication for life.
Cross-examination of Dr Ian will resume on Aug 26, followed by re-examination and the close of the defence case on the same day, he said. — Bernama

Title: Rehda Institute: One-size-fits-all RM300,000 housing cap needs rethink
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — Rehda Institute views positively the government’s indication that affordable housing may move away from the uniform RM300,000 price ceiling towards a more income-based model, saying affordability benchmarks should reflect local household incomes and actual demand.
The research arm of the Real Estate and Housing Developers’ Association (Rehda) said the benchmarks should be reviewed periodically, supported by income-based targeting and more location-specific allocation mechanisms.
“Furthermore, housing prices must also recognise actual delivery costs,” it said in a statement following the government’s decision to draft and amend four housing laws under the National Housing Policy (NHP) 2026-2035.
The institute noted that 82 per cent of developers surveyed in its Housing for All study reported that regulated prices for price-controlled housing were below actual development costs due to rising land, construction, labour, compliance and infrastructure costs.
It also supported the government’s emphasis on data-driven planning based on demographics, needs and actual demand.
Rehda Institute said better use of data on household formation, income, demographics, housing stock, vacancy rates, unsold completed units and mobility patterns could help address persistent supply-demand mismatches, unsold housing and abandoned developments.
“It can help avoid overbuilding in weak markets while ensuring genuine housing needs are met in areas of demand. Better data can also enable Malaysia to move from reacting to abandoned projects towards identifying risks earlier and preventing abandonment in the first place,” it said.
It also welcomed the NHP’s specific attention on the ageing population, including housing financing schemes tailored for senior citizens, retrofitting grants to facilitate ageing-in-place and incentives to the private developer for development of liveable senior care centres.
It said the approach was increasingly important as data from the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) showed that Malaysians aged 65 years and above accounted for eight per cent of the population in 2025, up from 7.6 per cent in 2024.
“Malaysia is on track to become an ‘aged nation’ by 2048, when citizens aged 65 and older reach 14 per cent of the total population. Future housing supply must respond to the different needs of households throughout their life cycle,” it noted.
On housing financing, the institute welcomed proposed measures including the Housing Credit Guarantee Scheme (SJKP), stepped financing, shared ownership and long-term fixed-rate mortgages, particularly as loan eligibility remains a key barrier for aspiring homeowners.
Moving forward, Rehda Institute said it would continue supporting the government through Training, Research and Education, including research and training collaborations and platforms such as the Malaysia-Cambridge Urban Platform (MCUP) to strengthen housing affordability measurement, big data analytics, urban planning and evidence-based policymaking.
In the same statement, Rehda Institute chairman Datuk Jeffrey Ng Tiong Lip was quoted as saying that the NHP 2026-2035 reflected many of the issues the institute had been advocating, particularly demand-driven supply, demographic responsiveness and more flexible financing.
“The next step is to ensure numerical targets remain guided by actual household needs. Ultimately, success should not simply be measured by how many homes are built or owned, but whether Malaysians have access to the right housing, in the right location, under a tenure and financial commitment that they can sustainably afford,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Prima facie proven: Court says Bandar Utama boy must enter defence in schoolmate’s murder
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Aug 13 — The High Court today ordered a 15-year-old boy to enter his defence on a charge of murdering a female student at a secondary school in Bandar Utama, Petaling Jaya, last year.
Judge Adlin Abdul Majid issued the order after finding that the prosecution had successfully established a prima facie case against the teenager.
Lawyer Kitson Foong, representing the accused, confirmed the court order to reporters after this morning’s proceedings.
The boy is accused of murdering the victim, who was 16 at the time, in the female students’ toilet at a national secondary school in Bandar Utama between 9.20am and 9.35am on Oct 14, 2025.
The charge was brought under Section 302 of the Penal Code, which carries the death penalty.
However, under Section 97(1) of the Child Act 2001, the death penalty cannot be imposed on offenders under 18 if convicted.
Instead, under Section 97(2) of the same Act, the court may order the offender to be detained for a period determined by the Yang di-Pertuan Agong, the Sultan, or the Yang di-Pertua Negeri.
So far, the prosecution has called three students, teachers, the victim’s mother, a pathologist and a senior investigating officer as witnesses.
The prosecution was conducted by deputy public prosecutors Raja Zaizul Faridah Raja Zaharudin, Aqharie Durranie Aziz and Ahmad Iqbal Aziz.
As the accused is still a minor and his identity cannot be disclosed, the entire proceedings were held in camera.
On Feb 12, the teenager pleaded not guilty after the charge was re-read to him in Mandarin before Judge Adlin.
On Jan 30, the prosecution obtained the Attorney General’s Chambers’ consent under Section 177A of the Criminal Procedure Code to transfer the case from the Petaling Jaya Magistrate’s Court to the Shah Alam High Court, after a psychiatric evaluation confirmed that the teenager was fit to stand trial.
On Oct 22, 2025, the teenager was charged in the Petaling Jaya Magistrate’s Court with the murder of his schoolmate, between 9.20am and 9.35am on Oct 14, 2025.
No plea was recorded at the time, however, as murder cases fall within the High Court’s jurisdiction.
The proceedings are ongoing. — Bernama

Title: Hoping for a downpour to wash away the smog? MetMalaysia says it won’t be enough for the next five days
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — The haze situation currently affecting the country is not expected to show any significant changes for the next three to five days, according to the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia).
MetMalaysia National Weather and Earthquake Operations Centre (POCGN) senior director Maqrun Fadzli Mohd Fahmi said that although rain is forecast to occur in several places, it is not yet able to restore air quality on a large scale.
“From the information we have so far, we have not seen a major change in the situation. We expect the situation to remain almost the same and in the next few days, there will be a little rain compared to the current dry conditions.
“We hope the rain will help, but if the air is very hazy, a little rain may not be able to remove the effects of the haze,” he said when interviewed on Bernama TV’s ‘Focus 15: Cross-Border Haze Threat.’
Commenting further, Maqrun Fadzli said the current haze situation is worse in the west and south of Sarawak, resulting in the closure of more than 100 schools in Serian yesterday, as well as affecting areas in the Peninsula including the Klang Valley.
Maqrun Fadzli said the main factor contributing to the situation is the Southwest Monsoon which usually occurs from May to September, which causes drier conditions and less rain.
“When we don’t get much rain, the weather will be hotter and this hot weather contributes to the risk of burning. From the burning, smoke and what we call haze are produced,” he said.
According to him, MetMalaysia constantly monitors hotspots using satellite images to identify forest fire areas before combining wind direction data to project the movement of smoke and suspended particles.
He said the information is used to identify areas with the potential to experience worse haze conditions and provide predictions of its movement.
Maqrun also advised the public to avoid open burning and reduce outdoor activities to avoid health risks due to unsatisfactory air quality.
As of this afternoon, data from the Malaysian Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal showed 10 areas recording unhealthy levels involving Samarahan, Serian, Kuching, Sri Aman, Sarikei, Mukah and Sibu in Sarawak, as well as Johan Setia (Selangor), Cheras (Kuala Lumpur) and Minden (Penang). — Bernama

Title: After calling in 115 witnesses and detaining seven suspects, MACC now weighs foreign forensic help to untangle Tabung Haji probe
Article:
KUCHING, Aug 13 — The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) is considering engaging foreign forensic experts to assist in its investigation into the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji.
MACC Chief Commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman said the investigation involves matters relating to investments, agreements and contracts, and therefore requires detailed forensic examination.
He said the examination would also cover meeting minutes and various documents relating to investment decisions.
“There are a large number of documents involved in this investigation that need to be reviewed and scrutinised. This requires specialised examination as well as expertise.
“Discussions on the appointment of forensic experts are also subject to the costs involved. The forensic experts will also work together with our specialist officers,” he told a press conference here today.
Meanwhile, Abd Halim said that to date, MACC had opened 14 investigation papers and taken several enforcement measures, including arrests, remands and seizures.
He said the investigations involved inspections and searches at 28 premises.
“A total of 115 witnesses have been called in for interviews and had their statements recorded at the MACC office, while seven suspects have been detained, five of whom were remanded,” he added. — Bernama

Title: If you have type O or AB blood, Johor’s Hospital Sultanah Aminah really needs you to come forward this weekend
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Aug 13 — Hospital Sultanah Aminah (HSA) has issued an urgent appeal for type O and AB blood donors as supplies of both types are running low.
In a Facebook post, the hospital’s Transfusion Medicine Department said donors can check the Johor Bahru Blood Donation Campaign Schedule page for locations.
Blood donation drives are also being held at the Johor Blood Donation Centre at Mid Valley Southkey today through Sunday, from 10am to 6.30pm; AEON Mall Bukit Indah today, Saturday, and Sunday from 10am to 3pm; and at the HSA Blood Donation Centre today and tomorrow from 8am to 4.30pm. — Bernama

Title: First AW189 helicopter lands as MMEA steps up patrols, rescues at sea
Article:
SUBANG JAYA, Aug 13 — The sovereignty of the country’s 556,285 square kilometres (km) of waters is now strengthened with the receipt of the first of four Medium Lift AW189 helicopters acquired for use by the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA).
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the helicopter would enhance the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency’s capabilities in carrying out aerial surveillance, enforcement, search and rescue (SAR) operations, medical evacuation (medevac) and special operations.
He said the acquisition of the sophisticated asset was important in facing the increasingly complex maritime security landscape, including the threat of cross-border crime, encroachment on fisheries resources and smuggling.
“Our maritime zone is very vast, so it is very important for the government to show a strong commitment to support enforcement agencies such as the MMEA,” he said at a press conference after the Malaysian Maritime AW189 Helicopter Reception Ceremony at the Subang Maritime Air Station here today.
Also present were Home Ministry secretary-general Datuk Dr Awang Alik Jeman and MMEA director-general Admiral Maritime Datuk Rosli Abdullah.
The procurement of four helicopters worth RM529 million was approved through the Fourth Rolling Plan of the Eleventh Malaysia Plan (11MP), under a five-year contract with manufacturer Leonardo.
The AW189 helicopter has an operating range of up to 1,166km and a maximum speed of 313km per hour, and can operate in various weather conditions while carrying five crew members and 14 passengers for rapid response operations at sea.
Saifuddin Nasution said the company had completed the project on schedule and the remaining three AW189 helicopters were expected to arrive in the country by the end of December.
“Apart from asset empowerment, focus is now also being given to developing personnel capacity to ensure they are skilled in operating the new aircraft’s sophisticated technology,” he said.
With the addition of the new helicopters, MMEA’s air fleet will increase from the current six helicopters to nine by the end of the year, further strengthening the agency’s record in guarding the country’s waters.
As of July 24, MMEA had carried out more than 116,192 inspections, with seizures valued at more than RM4.38 billion, while search and rescue operations had successfully rescued 638 victims in 129 cases.
Meanwhile, he said the government expected to receive another strategic asset, namely a mothership, in the first quarter of next year to further strengthen operations in the deep sea. — Bernama

Title: Two weeks of beatings, 29 injuries: Top court upholds death sentence for man who killed four-year-old stepson in Klang
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Aug 13 — The Federal Court today upheld the death sentence imposed on a former chef for the murder of his four-year-old stepson in 2015.
A three-member bench comprising Justices Datuk Rhodzariah Bujang, Datuk Che Mohd Ruzima Ghazali and Datuk Mohd Nazlan Mohd Ghazali dismissed Mohd Sazly Zamry’s final appeal against his conviction and sentence.
Justice Rhodzariah, delivering the unanimous decision, described the appellant’s killing of the innocent four-year-old boy as nothing short of heinous and diabolical.
She added that equally damning against the appellant was the pathologist’s undisputed evidence that the deceased had sustained 29 external injuries to his body and head, injuries that could not have been inflicted by anyone other than the appellant.
“The brutality perpetrated against the defenceless and innocent victim is beyond comprehension and is totally reprehensible, despicable and heinous, which shocked not only judicial conscience but also the collective conscience of our society,” she said.
Justice Rhodzariah said the death sentence was the only punishment commensurate with the crime committed by Mohd Sazly, 49.
Earlier, she stated that Mohd Sazly’s conviction was safe, as the prosecution had presented strong circumstantial evidence establishing his culpability beyond reasonable doubt.
Justice Rhodzariah said Mohd Sazly was the sole custodian of the deceased for two weeks at the material time, while his wife was at work. During that period, the deceased was subjected to constant verbal and physical abuse.
She further noted that Mohd Sazly had sought a neighbour’s help to dispose of the boy’s body, claiming that the child had been knocked down in an accident by a friend he refused to name.
He also resisted arrest and prevented his wife from opening the door when police arrived.
Mohd Sazly was convicted and sentenced to death by the Shah Alam High Court on Jan 17, 2020, for killing Aidil Adha, the son of his second wife, at a house in Jalan Sungai Udang, Klang, between 2pm and 6.15pm on Dec 20, 2015.
Subsequently, the Court of Appeal dismissed his appeal on April 14, 2023.
Witnesses testified that the victim was locked in a room for two weeks, with a rope tied from the inside to the outside of the door.
During that time, he was subjected to scolding and beatings. His body was later found in an unused toilet behind the house.
DNA from the victim was found on a cane and a mop handle, while mixed DNA was detected in blood splatters on the wall.
At today’s Federal Court hearing, deputy public prosecutor Eyu Ghim Siang argued for upholding the death sentence, emphasising the two weeks of sustained abuse.
Defence lawyer Datuk Rozal Azimin Ahmad, however, sought to have the sentence commuted to imprisonment. — Bernama

Title: Johor to add 5,000 smart CCTVs across Greater Johor Bahru in five years
Article:
PASIR GUDANG, Aug 13 – The Johor government plans to install 5,000 more smart closed-circuit television (CCTV) cameras across Greater Johor Bahru over the next five years to improve public safety, said State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor.
The cameras will be installed across four local authority areas as part of Johor’s push to become a Smart State through greater use of technology.
“We are targeting about 5,000 new smart CCTV cameras next year in the Greater JB region, that includes local authorities from the Johor Bahru City Council (MBJB), Pasir Gudang City Council, Iskandar Puteri City Council and Kulai Municipal Council.
“With the additional smart CCTV cameras, the residents and visitors will feel safer and this increases the overall well-being of the people,” he told reporters after officiating the Johor Smart City Forum 2026 at the Tunku Mahkota Ismail Youth Centre here today.
Mohd Jafni said the Johor government will also install more smart traffic lights in the state, especially in areas with high traffic flow rates such as in city centres and towns.
He said the use of such technology over the past few years have proven to be successful in managing a smooth traffic flow and reducing traffic congestion in an area.
“In addition, the state government will also install more smart street lights throughout the state for convenience,” he said, adding that the respective local authorities or contractors will be immediately notified of any issues with the smart lights where repair work can be carried out faster.
Earlier, Mohd Jafni announced that all 16 local authorities in the state had managed to obtain a rating of at least Level 1 for the Smart City category in the country.
“Most importantly, MBJB is the only local authority in the country to receive a Level 3 rating,” he said.
Johor is officially recognised as Malaysia’s first Smart State, achieving this milestone five years ahead of its 2030 target.
All 16 local authorities in the state have attained a Level 1 Smart City Early Adopter status, with MBJB leading the nation as the first local authority to reach Level 3 – Leading Smart City status.

Title: Johor wants to give stray dogs a better shot at life, Netherlands-style
Article:
PASIR GUDANG, Aug 13 — The Johor government plans to adopt the Netherlands’ widely cited approach to managing stray animals, including sterilisation, shelter care and adoption.
State Housing and Local Government Committee chairman Datuk Mohd Jafni Md Shukor said the state government would work with non-governmental organisations (NGOs) to address the stray dog and cat population.
“For stray dogs, the approach is similar to the one implemented in the Netherlands where the authorities spays the animal to eliminate unwanted litters, in addition to taking care of their welfare in terms of nutrition.
“So, the plan is to work closely with the NGOs that will place these stray dogs in a dedicated shelter instead of leaving them abandoned and emaciated,” he told reporters after attending the Johor Smart City Forum 2026 at the Tuanku Mahkota Ismail Youth Centre here today.
Mohd Jafni said the stray dogs would be neutered and properly cared for before being offered for adoption.
He said the state government welcomed the proposal and was prepared to work with relevant organisations.
At present, he said only the Johor Bahru City Council has a shelter for stray dogs in the district.
He said dogs caught by the council would be fed, treated and cared for before being offered for adoption.
“I will personally visit the shelter this September as I was told the facilities are almost ready,” he said.
Mohd Jafni said interactions with animal lovers during a previous campaign had also prompted suggestions for local authorities to take a more structured approach to managing stray dogs and cats.
He said this would require long-term efforts combining animal welfare measures with shelter care and adoption support.
The Netherlands has been widely credited with eliminating stray dogs from its streets through legislation and subsidised sterilisation programmes.
Its approach to managing stray dogs has been widely cited as a model for other countries, although free-roaming and feral cats remain an ongoing animal welfare and ecological challenge there.

Title: Transport Ministry to refer commingled oil tax issue to MOF for clarification
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 13 — The Transport Ministry will seek clarification from the Finance Ministry over concerns surrounding the tax treatment of commingled oil cargo, Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said today.
Loke said his ministry had yet to be informed of any new taxation involving such cargo, adding that the matter falls under the purview of the Royal Malaysian Customs Department and the Finance Ministry.
“This is something which is under Customs and under MOF. We will seek further clarification from MOF,” he told reporters after the Transport Ministry’s monthly assembly here today.
Loke was responding to concerns raised by maritime industry players over uncertainty surrounding the tax treatment of commingled oil cargo at Malaysian ports.
The issue has raised concerns among port businesses, with a maritime expert warning that uncertainty over the tax treatment could affect companies handling such cargo.
Commingling refers to the storage of different oil consignments together in the same shore tank before they are subsequently transferred or exported.
